title: Newly Single
essence: He leaves the party for an open-air rooftop club over Atlantis, all strobes and blue-pink light, where the dancers smear in shifted time and he stands still and empty. His soul, a glowing see-through copy of him, peels out and floats up, watches the whole city lit below, is set down on a white-hot plain at the equator of a giant planet, and is cooled by angels pouring ice baths; back in the club the same water lands on his body under the strobe. Haze fills the room, the soul comes home, he leans back and breathes it in, and ends on the ledge staring at far mountains, then walks out into a street where he glimpses the EX's back and cannot reach him.
palette_notes: Night #0d1630 and spire blue #3a6fd8 from the Ankhu sheet (cbb5e9c5 aerial, 646ab0f0 misty platforms, 993cc7a2 deck). Purple #9b5fd0 and pink #ff5fa8 are the disc-spires of 959cd1f5 and the treatment's 'blue and pink lights throughout the city'. Soul blue-white #bfe6f2 is the ice blue of the aerial 434b7bdd and the soul glow. Red plain #b0303a and white sun #fbf6ea from 7a904269 (the red ground under a white light). District orange #d36f46 for the one accent: the spark at the soul's head (world module: never on the flesh).

full_text.line: The soul has escaped my body for the moment and left him on the dance floor. He can now just be
flesh and bones, rejection and heartache hit differently when there are no feelings afloat.
I want my soul now to imagine my body pulsing and head throbbing from the music and empty on
a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. Let's watch strangers collide and spark electric
currents that gamut the mood, a good one. We want him to be the last one to leave, prolonging the
bitter refraction inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us. Now let us put my
soul in the middle of an open field at the equator of a planet much larger than my own
and much hotter. Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water out of the ice bath salted from the closest
moons from angels of the newest religions and its joys capturing my body transiting in a flash of
strobe lights. Their gracious cursor blessed me, only infinity will tell. Now bring my soul back
to my body to lean back, breathe in the smoke that now fills the room and tell myself how good
it is to finally get acquainted with the night, staring into unfamiliar yet relatable mountains
in the distance and wandering eyes and wandering thoughts within reach.

characters.design_notes: Two copies, never merged: the flesh is the solid puppet; the soul is the same cards printed on translucent acetate in pale blue-white with a hollow ring head, glow behind, flickering faster when anxious and slower when settled. insights: Never merge the two copies: even after the return keep both cards in frame, the soul printed on acetate over the body. The line never says they became one thing again.
Time shift is a frame-rate contrast: dancers on 2s and 3s with ghost doubles, the poet on 1s. Cheap in cut-out, and it reads instantly.
'Much hotter' is a subtraction: blow the sky away until the plain stands in white; do not add flames.
Intercut body and soul on the pour: the same water lands on both, which is how the poem's 'cool me down' connects two places.
The planet is a floor: a horizon so wide it barely curves; one red-white ground card and ticks, nothing scattered on it (open means empty).
Strobes: keep flashes under safe rates; let the haze and the colour carry the club instead.
The last stanza and the street beat bleed into 09 (Yet Heard): the EX's back through the crowd is the hinge.
Atlas: Ankhu's architecture is stems and crowns over a cloud bank; one cloud card that cuts every stem at the same height makes the rooftop club read as high without ever showing the ground.

Atlas: foundry/08-03 shows the soul as a stippled silhouette over the floor tiles; perforate the soul cards (pin-punched acetate) rather than only tinting them, so light passes through and the copy reads as hollow.
Atlas: the equator plain can reuse the red soil of the Night Field (views/071) pushed to white-hot light: the soul goes back to the ancestors' ground without a word.
future: The soul acetate set returns wherever the poet is beside himself (09, 11).
The rooftop and club crowd (club_dress/shirt/jacket) are reused in 09.
The night street with the EX walking away opens 09; the mountains seen from the rooftop are the horizon he rides toward in 10.
The top-down Atlantis print is reused for 10's dusk exit and 14's ending.
The angels can return in 11 New Day as a blessing image.

atlas.district_language: Ankhu Spires is Atlantis from above: mushroom-stem towers with flat platform crowns joined by bridges, gardens and laundry on the platforms, cloud below and clear sky above. In cardboard that is a vertical stack: a cloud bank card cutting every stem at the same height, platform crowns as flat discs on thin stems (dowel or rolled card), violet and blue underlight on the stems (coded gradient on the stem cards, #3f5375/#1c3148), warm lamp points on the crowns. The club is an open crown two platforms over from a laundry roof; bridges are thin cards with rail ticks. The salt line rides up the stems at 4/10 of their height, far above any flood: paint it as a pale band on every stem. Never show the ground in the club shots; the only ground the poem gets is the soul's red-white equator plain and, at the very end, the wet street. The red of the shaft is the only red in Ankhu; keep the club violet/blue/pink.

staging.name: The soul leaves the dancer
staging.shot: medium on POET on the pulsing tile floor (grid light box), strobe on alternating frames; the soul card (same poet cards printed on perforated pale-blue acetate) peels up from the chest; camera cranes up with it past the crown's rail and two stem cards with lamp cables into violet sky.

staging.name: Strangers collide; the last one to leave
staging.shot: overhead (soul POV): the dance floor as a disc with crowd silhouettes in a motion-smeared ring, slowly turning; two stranger cards brush and a coded spark flares; then a 360 orbit around the body as crowd cards are pulled off one by one until he is alone in a light ring.

staging.name: Soul over Atlantis / the open field at the equator
staging.shot: top-down aerial: the Atlantis print (06's round plaza at centre) lit blue and pink, cloud acetate drifting across, the soul small in the foreground layer; match-cut on the soul's silhouette to an extreme wide of the red plain, horizon a near-flat sag, a gas giant card filling the top third, white sun card back-lit; equator ticks along the ground.

staging.name: Angels' ice-water baptism
staging.shot: high angle looking down: three angel cards at three tilts on the rail above, basins tipping; braided water strips (clear acetate with white streaks, 4 replacement lengths) fall onto POET's upturned face; slow motion = hold each water state 3 frames; tight on the face as it hits, sunglasses beaded.

staging.name: Haze and the soul's return
staging.shot: haze acetate layers roll in over the floor (3 sheets sliding at different speeds); side light through them as beams; slow push to the chest as the soul card slides back down its own path and sinks under the torso card; the body leans back against the subwoofer wall, breathing in.

staging.name: Mountains from the rooftop
staging.shot: over-the-shoulder at the parapet: POET's back/shoulder card large at frame left, rail card, three mist layers, a pale mountain range card far off under a crescent moon; long-lens compression = the layers close together and barely parallaxing; his hand card reaches toward the ridge and stops short.
